context.content: I was born and raised in this city. I've grown to love it and be proud of it. Because I genuinely believe that Eindhoven is a city to be proud of. Yesterday though, that all went out the window. I went for a walk in the morning, nice little stroll down to Strijp-S to see the developments. I'd like to keep tabs on that, so to speak. Only to find out when I got back home, that the city centre basically turned into a 'no go zone'. I wasn't in the loop that one or two groups had announced protests. But these were forbidden by the local government. Pretty simple right? Shortly thereafter everything went tits up. The deeper I went into thiss rabbit hole of absolutely terrible news, the sadder I became. I understand that you have a right to protest. You can disagree what our central government has put into place to battle the corona epidemic. All fair. Your voice can be heard. But when you come to a city (not necessarily even living in it) just to cause mayhem, you've got a couple of screws loose and this surpasses your right to protest on a whole new level. These people were just out to battle with the police. Saying that the police instigated this violence is, in my book at least, complete BS. Being cooped up in your home for an elongated time isn't good for anyone, we know this. It puts a lot of stress on you and yes, I've feld down in the dumps at one point as well. With no reasonable end in sight. But does that mean than, that you have to tear down a whole city centre just to get your point across? Does it really benefit your cause when you flip and burn a car from the railway company? Does it really prove your point when you demolish and loot the local Jumbo supermarket? I'll answer that for you. No. It doesn't. It just ruins the reputation of those who are capable of peaceful protest (even more). And yes, like someone else mentioned in this subreddit, this is not how we normally do things around here. Or ever. I haven't felt as hopeless and sad as I did last night, watching these things unfold. I just don't get it. Can anyone help me perhaps? Because these people weren't there to protest against the curfew or the corona measures. In the beginning, maybe, but when the scum of the earth turn up to turn up the heat, that all changed rapidly. I still love my city, but common sense has faded. Completely. I've stayed indoors for as much as I can. I abide to the rules. But that doesn't mean that I'm a sheep. For some reason, I feel that, sometimes, I'm the only one to see the bigger picture. Why these measures are in place. Fun? No. Necessary? Yes. I firmly believe so. I've seen friends who work in hospitals go above and beyond to help those in need and suffer even more themselves. Burned out, worn down. But do you see me in despair, tearing up city blocks because I don't agree with something? No. Because I'm a civilized human being, able to look further ahead then my own flippin' nose. I just don't get it. I'm still sad. Rant over.
